# Welcome {.unnumbered} This is the website of **R for Audit Analytics**, a book on data analytics for auditors, using the free and open-source R language. It is free to read, for everyone. The book is written for auditors, in government and elsewhere, who want to analyse data themselves: to read the files an auditee gives them, clean and combine them, test them against rules, look for duplicates, gaps and unusual patterns, and turn the results into findings and reports. No knowledge of programming is assumed. Every technique is explained in plain language, and every one is shown at work on an audit problem, with Indian examples, amounts in lakh and crore, and the kind of data that auditors actually receive. ## What is in the book {.unnumbered} The book follows the course of an audit. It has nine parts. The first two teach R and how to get audit data ready. The rest are the audit toolkit, from looking at the data to the final report. | Part | What it covers | |-----------------------|------------------------------------------------| | [**I. R Foundations**](part1-foundations.qmd) | The R language. Objects, subsetting, functions, pipes, conditions and loops, and functional programming | | [**II. Getting Data Ready**](part2-data-ready.qmd) | Reading files, including PDFs and messy Excel. Cleaning, combining, transforming, joining and reshaping data. Dates, and data too large for Excel | | [**III. Working with Text Fields**](part3-text-fields.qmd) | Cleaning text, regular expressions, and validating PAN, GSTIN, Aadhaar and other identifiers | | [**IV. Exploring and Sampling**](part4-explore-sample.qmd) | Charts, factors, descriptive statistics, probability, audit sampling, and statistical tests | | [**V. Forensic Tests**](part5-forensic.qmd) | Rule-based validation, Benford's law, Nigrini's tests, duplicates, fuzzy matching, record linkage, gaps, and process mining | | [**VI. Modelling and Risk Scoring**](part6-risk-scoring.qmd) | Regression, logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, and data envelopment analysis | | [**VII. Finding Hidden Patterns**](part7-hidden-patterns.qmd) | Principal components, clustering, association rules, time series, and anomaly detection | | [**VIII. Beyond Tables**](part8-beyond-tables.qmd) | Text analytics, networks of related parties, and maps and geocoding | | [**IX. Reporting**](part9-reporting.qmd) | Reproducible audit reports and Excel working papers, generated from code | : The nine parts of the book {#tbl-parts} The appendices begin with the **Audit Question Finder**, which lists common audit questions and the section that answers each one. The other appendices list the datasets and the R packages used, and explain the choice of colours for charts. ## Where to start {.unnumbered} - **New to R?** Start with [Gearing Up](00-Zero.qmd), then read Parts I and II in order. - **Know some R already?** Go straight to Part V, *Forensic Tests*, or to the part your audit needs. - **Have an audit question?** Look it up in the [Audit Question Finder](audit-questions.qmd). [How to Use This Book](how-to-use.qmd) gives these paths in more detail, with a short course for a first audit and a list of chapters for each kind of audit. It also explains how the chapters are written. ## Software {.unnumbered} The book uses R version 4.5 and the RStudio editor, both free. The code makes full use of the *tidyverse* family of packages, and of the native pipe `|>`. The packages used in each part, with a single command to install all of them, are listed in @sec-packages. ## A note on data {.unnumbered} The author works for the Government of India. The opinions expressed in this book are personal to the author, and are not to be construed as those of the Government of India, or of the author in his official capacity. All datasets and examples in the book are either sample datasets available with R and its packages, open data available online, or data simulated by the author to demonstrate the case under discussion. All names of persons, firms, offices and places in the simulated data are made up. None of the datasets or examples pertains to any entity handled by the author in his official capacity, and nothing in the book breaches official secrecy in any manner. ## Licence and feedback {.unnumbered}
